title: KAKE NEWS INVESTIGATES: Duplicate license plate numbers lead to dangerous situations for some Kansas drivers

reports.title: KAKE NEWS INVESTIGATES: Duplicate license plate numbers lead to dangerous situations for some Kansas drivers

summary:
Matthew and Leah Spurlock were pulled over in Colwich, Kansas, after a Flock camera flagged their minivan as possibly stolen. Their KU Alumni plate had the number 7007, and a stolen GMC pickup had a temporary Kansas tag with the same number but a different background. Police learned the wrong plate type had been entered into the system. About a month later, in Catoosa, Oklahoma, another Flock camera led police to stop them. The Spurlocks said officers pointed guns at them and handcuffed Matthew.

Wichita police Captain Casey Slaughter said Flock cameras read only letters and numbers, not plate designs, so duplicate numbers can cause errors. Kansas has more than 100 plate designs, about half specialty plates, and it is moving from six digit to seven digit numbers to avoid duplicates. Wichita police have discussed training Flock to recognize plate backgrounds. The Spurlocks are no longer worried because the stolen vehicle entry expired, and they hope to keep their 14 year old plate.
